relationships.description: The collaborating roles jointly read, create or update the business object, such as a shared deal file or contract draft, while carrying out their collective work.
relationships.evidence: A process or RACI document for the joint activity lists the business object as an input or output handled by the collaboration, or a shared workspace or record shows edits by each participating role.

relationships.description: The business role is one of the participants whose joint membership makes up the collaboration, which dissolves if fewer than two such roles remain.
relationships.evidence: A governance charter, committee terms of reference or org model lists the role as a named member of the collaboration.

relationships.description: The collaboration is the joint actor that carries out the business interaction, with its member roles contributing parts that none could complete alone.
relationships.evidence: A process model or swimlane diagram assigns the interaction, such as joint deal approval, to the collaboration's pooled lane or to its named committee, and meeting minutes or sign-off records show its members completed it.

notes: The composes relationship to BusinessRole conflicts with ArchiMate semantics. Roles exist independently of any collaboration, so this is aggregation, not composition. The accesses relationship to BusinessObject is a derived shortcut. In ArchiMate, the access normally belongs to the BusinessInteraction the collaboration performs, not to the active structure itself.
